body:
## Problem

The URL Checker workflow is broken in two ways:

1. **The `gaurav-nelson/github-action-markdown-link-check` action is deprecated** — the repo is explicitly marked as deprecated and points to `tcort/github-action-markdown-link-check` as its successor.

2. **The successor action has a known bug** ([tcort/markdown-link-check#553](https://github.com/tcort/markdown-link-check/issues/553), [tcort/github-action-markdown-link-check#6](https://github.com/tcort/github-action-markdown-link-check/issues/6)) where `markdown-link-check` silently fails inside the Docker container, reporting all links as good without actually checking anything.

Additionally, the `check-modified-files-only` mode used for PRs has never worked correctly due to shallow clone (`fetch-depth: 1`) preventing `git diff` from finding changed files.

## Impact

- On `push` to master: the old action still works (using `markdown-link-check@3.8.7`), but this will stop receiving updates
- On `pull_request`: the modified-files check silently checks zero files and always passes — broken links are not caught until they reach master

## Fix

PR #3332 replaces the Docker-based action with a direct installation and invocation of `markdown-link-check@3.14.2` on the runner, which works correctly. It also fixes PR-level detection by using `fetch-depth: 0`.

## Security Review of `tcort/markdown-link-check` Dependency Chain Before adopting `markdown-link-check@3.14.2` (and the associated GitHub Action), a security review was performed on the package and its tcort-maintained dependencies. The review covers the npm packages that would run in our CI environment. ### Summary | Package | Version | Published Size | Install Hooks | `process.env` Access | `eval()`/`child_process` | Network Calls | npm ↔ GitHub Match | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `markdown-link-check` | 3.14.2 | 42.2 KB (5 files) | None | 1 (legitimate, documented) | None | Link checking only | ✅ Verified | | `link-check` | 5.5.1 | 19.1 KB (8 files) | None | None | None | Link checking only | ✅ Verified | | `markdown-link-extractor` | 4.0.3 | ~2 KB (1 file) | None | None | None | None | ✅ Verified | | `html-link-extractor` | 1.0.5 | ~2 KB (1 file) | None | None | None | None | ✅ Verified | **Verdict: No signs of malicious code or supply chain compromise in any package.** All packages are maintained by Thomas Cort (`tcort`), who has had a GitHub account since 2010, is the original author of `markdown-link-check` (created 2016, 685 stars), and is the sole npm publisher for all four packages.

markdown-link-check@3.14.2 (top-level package)

 - **Published files**: `index.js` (8.7 KB), `markdown-link-check` CLI (19.5 KB), `package.json`, `LICENSE.md`, `README.md` - **No install hooks** — only `pretest` and `test` scripts, which do not run on `npm install` - **`process.env` access**: One instance in `index.js` (~line 34). This powers the documented `{{env.VAR_NAME}}` replacement feature for templating environment variables into HTTP headers/URL patterns (e.g., auth tokens). The variable name is restricted by regex `/[a-zA-Z0-9\-_]+/` and values are only used locally in string replacements. Not exfiltrated anywhere. - **No `eval()`, `Function()`, `child_process`, base64, obfuscated code, or unexpected network calls** - **Runtime dependencies**: `async`, `chalk`, `commander`, `link-check`, `markdown-link-extractor`, `needle`, `progress`, `proxy-agent`, `xmlbuilder2` — all well-known, widely-used packages - **npm tarball SHA256 verified** as byte-for-byte match with GitHub source at v3.14.2 tag

link-check@5.5.1

 Every line of all 8 published JS files was read and analysed: - `index.js` (32 lines) — dispatches to protocol-specific handlers - `lib/BlackHole.js` (14 lines) — Writable stream that discards data - `lib/LinkCheckResult.js` (14 lines) — simple data class - `lib/proto/hash.js` (10 lines) — anchor link checker, pure logic - `lib/proto/file.js` (21 lines) — `file://` URL checker using `fs.access()` - `lib/proto/http.js` (124 lines) — HTTP HEAD/GET requests via `needle`, with retry logic for 429s - `lib/proto/https.js` (3 lines) — re-exports `./http` - `lib/proto/mailto.js` (35 lines) — email validation via MX lookup **Comprehensive grep for dangerous patterns across all files:** | Pattern | Matches | |---|---| | `process.env` | 0 | | `child_process` / `exec` / `spawn` | 0 | | `eval(` / `Function(` | 0 | | `base64` / `Buffer.from` / `atob` / `btoa` | 0 | | `crypto` (mining) / `WebSocket` / `net.connect` | 0 | - **Dependencies**: `needle`, `ms`, `proxy-agent`, `node-email-verifier`, `is-relative-url` (declared but unused — minor hygiene issue). All well-known packages. - **npm tarball verified** as matching GitHub source at v5.5.1 tag

markdown-link-extractor@4.0.3

 The entire package logic is 13 lines of code in `index.js`: ```javascript const { marked } = require('marked'); const htmlLinkExtractor = require('html-link-extractor'); module.exports = function markdownLinkExtractor(markdown, extended = false) { marked.setOptions({ mangle: false }); const html = marked(markdown); const links = htmlLinkExtractor(html); return links; }; ``` - **No install hooks, no `process.env`, no `eval()`, no `child_process`, no network calls, no obfuscation** - **Dependencies**: `marked` (36k stars, the standard Node.js markdown parser) and `html-link-extractor` (also by tcort, reviewed below) - **npm tarball verified** as byte-for-byte match with GitHub source at v4.0.3 tag

html-link-extractor@1.0.5

 36 lines of code. Uses `cheerio` to extract `href`/`src` attributes from HTML tags (`a`, `img`, `iframe`, `video`, `audio`, `source`, `embed`, `track`, `area`, `link`, `input`). - **No install hooks, no `process.env`, no `eval()`, no `child_process`, no network calls, no obfuscation** - **Sole dependency**: `cheerio` (the de-facto standard Node.js HTML parser) - **npm tarball verified** as matching GitHub source

Residual risks and recommendations

 1. **Mutable `v1` tag on the GitHub Action**: If using `tcort/github-action-markdown-link-check`, pin to a commit SHA rather than `@v1` to prevent silent changes. (PR #3332 installs the npm package directly, avoiding this.) 2. **Single maintainer**: `tcort` is the sole npm publisher for all four packages. This is a bus factor / account compromise risk, but there is no indication of compromise and this is standard for most GitHub Actions and npm packages. 3. **npm install at runtime**: The action runs `npm i -g markdown-link-check@3.14.2` at runtime. While the version is pinned, npm does not provide the same immutability guarantees as container image digests. No npm provenance attestations are published yet (tracked in tcort/markdown-link-check#544). 4. **Transitive dependencies not deeply audited**: Direct dependencies of the tcort packages are all well-known (`marked`, `cheerio`, `needle`, `proxy-agent`, `async`, `chalk`, `commander`, etc.), but their own transitive dependency trees were not individually reviewed. 5. **Node.js base image**: The Docker-based action uses `node:21.7.3-alpine3.18` which is EOL (tracked in tcort/github-action-markdown-link-check#5). This is a maintenance concern for the action, not directly relevant if installing the npm package directly as in PR #3332.
